correctness.rationale: For any five-vertex dominating set, \(a+b=5\) and \(9-b\le3a,\ 9-a\le3b\) force splits 2+3 or 3+2. Tight neighborhood capacity implies disjoint selected-point line sets (same class), or disjoint selected-line point sets (\(x-y\) parallel class); all remaining selected vertices are forced. Conversely all 9+9 selections dominate by the TD(3,3) incidence rule. Distance-four classes yield 18 distinct canonical sets, a unique triple-dominated centre, and vertex transitivity gives one orbit. Standalone code checks every 262144 subset plus a distinct LCF graph isomorphism, without substituting finite data for the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The projective-plane theorems require a full projective plane of order q (q^2+q+1 points and the same number of lines). value.rationale: The classical Pappus graph is a canonical cubic symmetric incidence graph whose domination number five was already catalogued. The complete 18-set classification, dual point-line structural characterization, exact closed-neighborhood multiplicities and one orbit are natural finite exact facts not forced by that scalar and useful for optimal sensor placement equivalence and symmetry-reduced incidence covering. The result is self-contained and structural rather than arbitrary unmotivated parameter recomputation.
